title: How big is the next stack of squares?
description: A stack of little squares has three rows of three, and the next stack is found by adding a row and a column. The next stack has four rows of four. Keeko doubts this and says the stack adds only one more row of three.
teaching_notes: One idea: each stack grows by one row and one column, so it stays a square and its side goes up by one. Watch for students who add only a row and get a rectangle.

source: A stack of squares is 3 by 3 little squares. What is the next stack, and how many little squares does it have?
video_script.why: The child learns how a stack of squares grows from one shape to the next and counts the little squares in the new stack, as in the stacked squares of the book.
video_script.substitution: The stack before is three by three little squares.
video_script.anchor: a stack of three rows of three little squares, with an empty frame for the next stack
video_script.wrong_answer: the next stack has twelve little squares
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the next stack has twelve little squares, since it adds one more row of three. Twelve little squares make four rows of three, which is a rectangle and not a square stack, so the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: The next stack is four by four, with sixteen little squares

final_answer.value: a 4 by 4 stack with 16 little squares
final_answer.spoken: a four by four stack with sixteen little squares

maths_rules: a stack of squares has as many rows as columns
to go to the next stack add one row and one column, so the side goes up by 1: 3 + 1 = 4
the next stack is 4 rows of 4 little squares
video_script.design: The three by three stack stays on the board. A new row and a new column slide in and the stack is counted again.
